rv.q: It is a tidy, colorful production with a strong cast and engaging characters.
The big number arrives, characters emote, high notes ring and ring and ring again … and the aria subsides unmemorably, without leaving the ozone tang that signals a bolt of musical lightning.

Like a skipping stone, Bates’s adaptation bounces across Chabon’s novel while never really plunging into it, for a treatment that is both too much for opera and not enough: too much plot, not enough transcendence.
It soars in the superhero realm, devastates in the human one, and, most importantly, offers an accessibility that won’t send newcomers to the opera running for the exit.
Art like "Adventures of Kavalier and Clay" is what allows us to do so.
As a Gesamtkunstwerk, it succeeded brilliantly.

Bolstered by the efforts of a committed cast, Mason Bates’s Kavalier & Clay is a reasonably enjoyable time, but it never delves beneath the surface level of its source text and never really justifies its own existence.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this ambitious operatic adaptation of Chabon's sprawling novel, praising its timely themes and emotional resonance while questioning whether the complex, densely-plotted source material suits opera's need for simplicity.

vr.q: if you love opera this production is so fresh and innovative and if you've never been to an opera this is the perfect entry point
